ground_truth: Explain why we have seasons. In your response, the word "sun" must appear at least three times, and the explanation should be exactly four sentences long.
bot_response: We  have seasons because of the  tilt of Earth's axis. As  Earth orbits aroun d the sun, different  parts of our  planet are tilted towar d or away from the sun at different times  of the year. When  your part of Earth is tilted toward the sun , the sun's rays  hit more directly and stay  in the sky longer during the  day, making it warmer. That 's summer. When your part of  Earth is tilted away from the sun , the rays come in at  a lower angle and there are  fewer hours of daylight, so  it's colder. That's winter. Spring  and fall happen in  between when the  tilt is more  neutral relative to the sun.  It's worth  noting that this  tilt is permanent  and stays  at about the  same angle as  Earth orbits,  which is why we get  this predictable cycle  of seasons every  year.
